STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white flat plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner bowl wall. Square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate here looks medium-sized, a standard dinner plate, so about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the bacon strip is roughly 11-12 cm long and the plate's side spans about 2.3 of those lengths, giving about 25-27 cm.
Both cues agree. Width ≈ 25 cm, so area ≈ 25 x 25 = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: it covers roughly 30% of the plate, about 190 cm². The clumps are about 1.5 cm thick on average (small curds stacked about two deep at the thickest points, averaging around half the peak). Volume ≈ 190 x 1.2 ≈ 230 ml. Bulk density 0.8 g/ml gives ≈ 180 g.
- Bacon: about 3 strips, total around 30 g, thin and flat.
- Sautéed greens (snap peas or green beans with carrot shreds): a loose heap covering about 15% of the plate, roughly 95 cm², averaging about 1.5 cm thick. Volume ≈ 140 ml. Cooked greens at 0.6 g/ml gives ≈ 85 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: Nothing sits under the items; the plate is flat and the food lies directly on the surface. No hidden base layer is added.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (as served):
- Scrambled egg (with some butter/oil): about 150 kcal.
- Bacon, cooked: about 540 kcal.
- Cooked green vegetables with a little oil: about 60 kcal.

Totals: egg 180 g ≈ 270 kcal; bacon 30 g ≈ 160 kcal; greens 85 g ≈ 50 kcal. Total ≈ 295 g and about 480 kcal.
